items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: And he wrote 'Turquoise Cloud' for Kay Davis to sing, you know.

ctx.x: And he wrote 'Turquoise Cloud' for Kay Davis to sing, you know. But anything the man wrote, I'm sorry, there's nothing you can say about it. He was in a class all by himself. The man could take blues and make a symphony out of it, because there was more 12-bar choruses in that book, but when you heard it it really didn't altogether sound exactly blues. There was composition -- descriptive music. Everything in there it described somebody's life or described a happening. It was all descriptive music, you see.
And he would know just which man to pick to give him the solo to play that he knew they would describe it like he wanted it described. That's what kind of a creative mind he had, you see.
